one_month_reasoning: The one big scheduled event in the window is Q3 2026 earnings before the open on 2026-10-29 (source 44). The bar has come down: Zacks consensus is EPS $9.83 and revenue $22.08B (source 37), below Q2's $23.0B (source 2). Lilly beat Q2 EPS by a wide margin ($8.38 vs $6.01, source 38). Industry data from the quarter point to another volume beat. Lilly says about 700k seniors started GLP-1s under the Medicare Bridge, with about 70% on Lilly drugs (sources 23, 24). Foundayo reached about 47.5k weekly scripts in the week of Sep 11, up from 34k in early August (sources 6, 40), and wins over 30% of new oral patients (source 22). Lilly holds about 61% of US obesity scripts (source 25). On the other side, Zepbound's CVS return on 2026-10-01 trades volume for price (sources 9, 39), and Q4 or early 2027 commentary may show more US price erosion. Novo reports on 2026-11-04, after the window. A CagriSema FDA decision is expected around late 2026 and could land inside it (source 43). The stock fell about 3% in the two sessions after the EloraTZP data (sources 28, 37) and is about 11% below its 52-week high. I set the median at about $1,160 (+0.9%) with roughly 10.5% one-month vol (35%/3.5, plus a small earnings-day add). The spread stays close to symmetric because the earnings reaction can go either way.

fair_value.method: P/E on the earnings the market will price in October 2027: NTM EPS about $55 (2028E) x 22x = $1,210, weight 70%. Cross-check: the 30-analyst mean target of $1,329 with a 10% optimism haircut = $1,196, weight 30%. Blend = about $1,205, about 5% above the $1,149.85 close.

methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Oct-2027 (approx. 2028E) $55 x 22x forward P/E

inputs_detail.derivation: Underlying 2026 EPS is about $39.8 (consensus $36.8 plus $3.03 IPR&D). Moving to 2027 consensus of $47.5 is about +19%. I assume about +16% in 2028. On volume: the US branded obesity market grew 85% in Q1 per Novo; Lilly holds about 61% share and about 70% of new Medicare starts; the Bridge now runs to 2027-12-31. On price: Q2 US price was -9% ex-rebate adjustments; Novo's Wegovy list price drops to $675 in January 2027; CVS gets double-digit savings; the $245 Medicare net price applies; BGH says 10% of employers who cover GLP-1s plan to drop them in 2027. 47.5 x 1.16 = about $55.

Today's price / 2027 consensus = 24.2x (Zacks shows 32x on its NTM basis). I assume about 2 turns of compression by Oct-2027 as growth slows toward the mid-teens. By then the market will be looking at 2028, when three risks sit closer: the Medicare Bridge expires with BALANCE Part D indefinitely delayed; MariTide Phase 3 data arrive in early 2027; and Paragraph IV generic litigation is under way. The litigation should not bring a generic inside the horizon, because the compound patent runs to 2036 and the 30-month stays apply, but it caps the terminal multiple.

bear.story: The price war spreads. Novo's $675 Wegovy list price in January 2027, PBM and CVS concessions, more employers dropping coverage (BGH: 10% of current coverers plan to drop in 2027), and the $245 Medicare price push US net price down 15-20% a year. Investors start to price a post-2027 Medicare cliff because BALANCE is indefinitely delayed. Strong MariTide Phase 3 data in early 2027 or a CagriSema approval make the incretin class look crowded, and Paragraph IV headlines weigh on the terminal value. 2027 EPS comes in around $44, the market looks through to flat 2028, and the multiple falls to about 17x on $47.

base.story: Volume keeps outrunning price. Lilly holds about 60% of US obesity scripts and about 70% of new Medicare starts. Foundayo moves from about 20% to about 30% of oral scripts and expands to 40+ markets, and Mounjaro grows abroad despite NRDL pricing. 2027 EPS is about $47-48 and NTM about $55, valued at about 22x. The retatrutide BLA is filed in Q1 2027 and EloraTZP enters Phase 3, keeping the pipeline premium.

bull.story: Foundayo's new-patient share (over 30% and growing week on week) turns into a real share of total oral scripts. Medicare uptake keeps compounding and CMS signals permanent Part D coverage. Retatrutide gets priority review with approval visible for late 2027 or early 2028, EloraTZP Phase 3 starts, and MariTide data underwhelm. Volume growth swamps price erosion, 2027 EPS beats to $50+, NTM EPS is about $60, and the multiple holds at about 27x. This lines up with Citi's $1,600 target.

thesis_break_reason: Near $820 (about -29%, under the bear multiple on consensus 2027 EPS) the market would most likely be pricing a structural break rather than 35%-vol noise. Candidates: US tirzepatide net price collapsing toward the $245-350/month Medicare and TrumpRx levels across commercial channels; Medicare obesity coverage ending after the Bridge expires on 2027-12-31 with no successor; a lasting share loss to the Wegovy pill, CagriSema or MariTide; a retatrutide regulatory or safety setback; or an adverse early ruling in the Paragraph IV litigation that threatens the 2036 compound patent.

reasoning: This continuation added about 35 searches and page reads, mostly in the industry lane. The new chain evidence mostly confirms round 1's picture of a durable volume lead with steadily falling price, with a few changes. (1) Volume is better than I had: about 700k Medicare Bridge starts with about 70% on Lilly drugs (up from 600k), Lilly holding about 61% of US obesity scripts against Novo's 39%, and Foundayo taking over 30% of new oral patients, with weekly scripts up from about 34k to about 47.5k. The Wegovy pill is about flat at about 183k, so Foundayo's share of oral scripts has risen from about 17% to about 21%. (2) The coverage outlook is mixed. CMS extended the Bridge through 2027-12-31 but indefinitely delayed BALANCE Part D, which creates a 2028 cliff the market will be weighing by October 2027. Employers are tightening: per BGH, 10% of those who cover GLP-1s plan to drop them in 2027. (3) There is a new structural headline: 14 Paragraph IV ANDA filers, sued by Lilly on 2026-08-07. The compound patent runs to 2036 and 30-month stays apply, so this is a terminal-multiple issue, not a 12-month revenue risk. (4) The pipeline was confirmed: retatrutide BLA in Q1 2027 (Polymarket gives 4% to approval in 2026 on $591k volume, consistent with that timing), and EloraTZP showed 23.3% weight loss vs 14.8% for tirzepatide but with 11-27% discontinuation; the stock rose 0.5% on the data. (5) Consensus is little changed: 2027 EPS $47.51, mean target $1,329. On balance the bullish volume evidence and the bearish coverage and generic headlines roughly offset, so I keep NTM EPS at $55 x 22x = $1,210, blended with the haircut target of $1,196 for a fair value of about $1,205. The scenario mean is about $1,220. Distribution: a lognormal with median about $1,200 and sigma 0.33, with a slightly fattened left tail for a price-war or coverage-cliff shock. Correction to round 1: the stock was not down 7% over the past month; Zacks shows +2.1% over the month to 2026-09-30, with a roughly 3% pullback in the two sessions after the EloraTZP data. CNBC and Fierce pages were blocked, so I used figures quoted by other outlets and labelled them. The Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage estimate endpoints were unavailable (plan or rate limit), so consensus comes from StockAnalysis and Zacks.
